content_of_post_to_answer: Do INTPs really struggle to focus on tasks if they have an unanswered question in their mind? How do they deal with it?
answer: The interesting part is that the unanswered question is not always a distraction; for many INTPs it represents an unfinished mental model. Their attention keeps returning because the brain is trying to resolve inconsistency, not because they lack discipline. The challenge is learning when a question needs solving now and when it can be parked. A simple note can act as a temporary closure: the mind often releases a problem once it knows the question has not been forgotten. Curiosity becomes a strength when it is managed, not when it is allowed to control the entire day.
